prompt_text: What is the best Airbnb or short term rental to book in Nashville for a family of four?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but to give the single best recommendation I need a few details. Quick questions:

- What are your travel dates (or month)?  
- What’s your budget per night (or total)?  
- Do you want to be close to downtown/ Broadway, or prefer a quieter neighborhood/suburb?  
- Do you need parking or a car? Ages of the kids? Any must-haves (crib, fenced yard, pool, kitchen, washer/dryer, accessibility)?

While you answer, here are practical tips and neighborhood suggestions so you can find an ideal family rental right away.

What to look for (Airbnb filters to use)
- Entire home or entire apartment (privacy, kids can roam).  
- At least 2 bedrooms or 3 beds (so everyone sleeps comfortably).  
- Amenities: kitchen, washer/dryer, air conditioning, free parking (driveway/garage), self check-in.  
- Family-friendly items: crib/pack-n-play, high chair, fenced yard (if young kids).  
- Safety and quiet: look for listings that explicitly say “family/kid friendly” and read reviews for noise and safety.  
- Good host track record: high review score, responsive host, lots of reviews.  
- Cancellation and cleaning fee details — these affect total cost.

Best neighborhoods for a family of four
- 12South — walkable, lots of family restaurants and parks; charming houses and boutiques; easy for family strolls.  
- Germantown — close to downtown but calmer than Broadway; great restaurants and newer renovated homes.  
- East Nashville — artsy, neighborhood parks, more single-family homes and yards; good for kids.  
- Green Hills / Hillsboro Village — suburban feel, good shopping (The Mall at Green Hills), quieter evenings.  
- Opryland/Donelson — great if you want easy access to Opry, airport, and larger houses with yards; more car-dependent but family-oriented.  
- Franklin (20–30 minutes south) — historic small-town feel with lots of family homes; quiet and very family-friendly.

Price expectations (approximate)
- Weeknights in off-season: many 2–3 bedroom homes or condos $120–250/night.  
- Weekends/peak season/special events (CMA Fest, big concerts): $250–600+ /night.  
- Suburban single-family homes with yard/pool: $200–450/night typical, higher during events.

Red flags to avoid
- Few or no reviews, especially for a newly listed “entire home.”  
- Excessive cleaning or additional guest fees that blow up the total cost.  
- Reviews mentioning noise all night, unsafe street, or inaccurate descriptions/photos.  
- Listings that limit check-in times (inconvenient with kids/late flights).

Booking tips
- Filter for “entire place,” 2+ beds, and family-friendly amenities. Sort by “Superhost” or high rating.  
- Message the host before booking to confirm sleeping layout, crib availability, and parking. Save that message in case of later issues.  
- Book early for popular weekends and CMA Fest (availability disappears months ahead).  
- Consider booking refundable/free-cancel options if plans might change.

If you tell me dates, budget, and neighborhood preference (downtown vs quiet), I’ll recommend 3–5 specific listings that match.
